previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with suprapubic abdominal pain and constipation. He has a chronic indwelling Foley catheter due to hypotonic bladder and a history of multidrug-resistant UTIs. Initial concern for UTI led to a short course of cefepime, but urine culture was negative and findings suggested inflammation from catheter change rather than active infection. Abdominal pain improved after bowel movements following enema use. A CT scan revealed malposition of the Foley catheter balloon in the prostate and a stable right renal mass being monitored for possible renal cell carcinoma. His oxygen saturation remained around 90-93% on room air, consistent with baseline asbestosis. He was discharged home with instructions to continue Macrobid prophylaxis, maintain regular catheter changes, and follow up with urology for ongoing management.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with hypotonic bladder with chronic foley and multiple drug 
resistant UTIs, CAD s/p CABG, s/p bovine AVR, T2DM, and HTN who 
presents with burning and itching at the site of his catheter  
  
# UTI: Patient complained of itching/burning starting at the 
site of his Foley catheter as well as suprapubic pain prior to 
admission.  UA at admission was suggestive of a UTI.  He was 
started empirically on vanc/cefepime given his history of drug 
resistant gram positive and negative infections.  His urine 
culture ultimately grew Acinetobacter and Enterobacter which 
were both susceptible to Cipro, the latter of which was found to 
be resistant to cefepime.  His Foley was changed on ___ once 
he was on appropriate antiobics given the UCx results.  He will 
complete a 14 day course of Cipro after discharge to a rehab 
facility.  He received pyridium for symptom control for a total 
of 3 days, which he will not continue at rehab.  His urologist 
was contacted regarding his frequent UTIs and chronic foley and 
he will follow-up with his urologist after discharge.  He should 
also be referred to infectious disease as an outpatient for 
consideration of suppressive antibiotics for his recurrent UTIs. 
 Of note, his daughter was contacted during this admission and 
stated she was concerned about Mr. ___ poor hygiene at 
home, which may be in part responsible for his recurrent UTIs 
with a variety of different organisms.
  
# AMS: Patient appeared disoriented and somewhat confused at 
admission.  This had resolved by the next morning where he was 
found to be A&Ox3 and alert.  This was thought to be from 
sundowning as his mental status improved after only one dose of 
antibiotics, making this change in mental status unlikely to be 
from his UTI.  He often reported feeling unwell but was unable 
to be more specific, which his daughter reports was happening at 
home as well prior to admission.  His VS were stable at these 
times, EKG was normal and there were no concerning objective 
findings.
  
# Hypoxia: He has a chronically elevated left hemidiaphragm and 
O2 sats during prior admissions have been in the low ___ on room 
air.  He remained in the high ___ to low ___ on room air during 
this admission.  A chest X-ray showed a chronically elevated 
left hemidiaphragm, small left sided effusion with no evidence 
of infection.
  
# Coronary artery disease s/p CABG and stenting: No chest pain 
during this admission and EKG was at baseline.  He was continued 
on his home aspirin, isosorbide mononitrate, metoprolol and 
statin.
  
# Hypertension: He remained normotensive and was continued on 
his home metoprolol and isosorbide mononitrate.

# Renal mass: Patient has known renal mass which is being 
followed with periodic imaging by urology.  Presumed to be renal 
cell carcinoma based on imaging characteristics, but no 
aggressive treatment is being pursued per family and outpatient 
providers.

# HLD: Continued on his home atorvastatin
  
# Diabetes: Diet controlled at home, blood sugar remained well 
controlled during this admission.  He was covered with an 
insulin sliding scale as an inpatient.

# Depression: Continued on his home citalopram and trazodone.

#Code status this admission: DNR/DNI (confirmed with daughter at 
admission)

urinary tract infection.  Study is to evaluate if there is an additional
pulmonary component.

recent ___.

TECHNIQUE:  AP upright and lateral chest radiographs.

FINDINGS:  There is stable elevation of left hemidiaphragm with a
corresponding left lower lobe atelectasis.  There is mild right lower lobe
atelectasis.  There has been interval increase in left pleural effusion. 
Cardiomediastinal silhouette is obscured by pleural effusion.  Moderate
multilevel degenerative changes of the thoracic spine are noted.  Patient is
status post sternotomy with sternotomy wires in unchanged vertical alignment
with no obvious hardware complications.

IMPRESSION:  Worsening left pleural effusion. No clear evidence of infection. 
Stable right basilar atelectasis and elevation of left hemidiaphragm.
